q1: SELECT CLASS FROM COURSES GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(*)>=5
q2: SELECT CLASS FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT STUDENT, CLASS FROM COURSES ) T GROUP BY CLASS HAVING COUNT(CLASS) >= 5

explanation: Q1 groups by CLASS and checks if the count of rows (i.e., students) in each class is >= 5. Q2 first removes duplicate student-class pairs, then groups by CLASS and checks if the count of distinct classes is >= 5. The difference lies in the GROUP BY and HAVING conditions.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least 5 students in the same class, but when duplicates are removed, the count of distinct classes should be less than 5.
